name: Dashboarding Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in dashboarding work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in dashboarding work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Re-check edge cases relevant to dashboarding (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
2. Surface known limitations of a chosen dashboarding approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
3. Keep dashboarding outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
4. Prefer explicit, readable dashboarding solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
5. When dashboarding decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
6. Measure before optimizing any dashboarding bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
7. Validate dashboarding outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic dashboarding advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of dashboarding correctness.
- Do not silently drop dashboarding edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting dashboarding assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.
- Avoid introducing new dashboarding abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these dashboarding guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
